paragraphs.text: Screenshot in, working UI out: several agents rebuild the same reference interface in parallel, and
you adopt the live result you like best. A DeepSeek Harness plugin.
Screenshot in. Working UI out.
Paste a screenshot of any interface. Run /clone 3. Three agents rebuild it in parallel,
each in its own isolated directory. A live panel shows the reference beside every attempt,
rendered and scored. You adopt the page that looks right — and it is already a working page.
→ Open a real clone in the browser
built by this plugin from this screenshot · 92.7% picture match
## The 30-second version
[代码示例省略，未执行]
No build step, no dependencies, no server. The adopted page is plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JS.
## Why this exists
A screenshot is the most precise specification a person can give. Every other input loses informatio
n: a paragraph drops the spacing rhythm, the type scale, the alignment of every block; a component l
ist drops the picture.
The usual flow is still: describe it, get one attempt, describe the differences, get another attempt
. One attempt is a lottery — you cannot tell whether the model misunderstood you or simply chose a d
ifferent solution, because you only ever see one.
`dsh-clone` changes the cost of being wrong. Three or four builders see the same reference and work
the same problem from different angles, every delivered page is rendered and compared with the refer
ence, and you keep the best.
| Lane strategy | What that builder is told to do |
| **Measure first** | write a layout spec — regions, grid, spacing scale, sampled hex palette, type

scale — then build strictly to it |
| **Structure first** | the whole page as semantic HTML first, t

hen style region by region from the outside in |
| **Visual first** | reproduce the picture first —

surfaces, type, spacing, silhouette — then add only the behaviour the image implies |
| **Component
first** | find the 5-8 reused parts, define each once, compose the page from them |
## Demo
Real runs, not mocks: one command each, no retries, no hand edits. Every page is a static file — ope
cks: one command each, no retries, no hand edits. Every page is a static file — open it and it runs.
| Reference | The clone, rendered by the plugin | Result |

|  |  | **91.9% match** · 1280×800 · two lanes raced, the better one adopted · open it |
|  |  | **9

1.9% match** · 1280×800 · one lane · open it |
|  |  | **97.8% match** · 520×360 · one file · open i
The dashboard and the landing page are the interesting ones: a sidebar, KPI cards with sparklines, a
layered area chart, a donut, a data table; glass panels over a gradient mesh, a feature grid and a
footer. Both were rebuilt from a single screenshot.
The score is the plugin's own, and it has three parts: both images are averaged into a coarse colour
grid, the colour comparison forgives a small uniform shift, and a separate **structure** term compa
res where the detail sits. The mix measures *how much of the picture agrees*, not whether the page i
s correct — two unrelated dark interfaces land around 58%, a faithful rebuild above 90%. See Honest
ct — two unrelated dark interfaces land around 58%, a faithful rebuild above 90%. See Honest limits.

## Usage
Paste a screenshot into the conversation, then:
| Command | What it does |

| `/clone` | 3 lanes rebuild the last image in this conversation |
| `/clone 4` | four lanes — maxim

al spread of approaches |
| `/clone 2 darker, mobile-first` | two lanes plus a note every builder mu

st honour |
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
**The gate comes first.** A page is measured only after it passes a deterministic, model-free checkl
ist: every local reference exists (no 404s), nothing fetches from a CDN, no placeholder copy, images
carry `alt`, form controls carry labels, and the document has a language and a title. A lane that f
ails is kept for inspection, shown with the failing checks, and **cannot be adopted** — however high
t for inspection, shown with the failing checks, and **cannot be adopted** — however high it scored.
**Isolation.** Each lane gets its own directory. Inside a git repository that is a real `git worktre
e` on its own branch (`dsh-clone/<id>-lane-<n>`), so nothing leaks between attempts and nothing touc
hes your working tree. Outside a repository it is a plain directory under `.dsh-clone/<id>/lane-<n>/
`. Existing `node_modules`, `.venv` and `vendor` are symlinked into each lane instead of reinstalled
. Existing `node_modules`, `.venv` and `vendor` are symlinked into each lane instead of reinstalled.
**The builders.** Each lane is a subagent with one job: read the reference image, then ship `index.h
tml` plus any local CSS/JS/assets. The delivery contract is identical for every lane and non-negotia
plus any local CSS/JS/assets. The delivery contract is identical for every lane and non-negotiable:
> no build step · no network at runtime · no CDN · no placeholder copy · fill the viewport · approxi
mate every image with CSS/SVG · leave no scratch files
The strategies differ; the contract does not. Every lane also carries an explicit effort budget (≈20
-25 tool calls) and a wall-clock limit: a builder that keeps polishing is stopped, and whatever it a
lready wrote is delivered and scored instead of stalling the clone.
**The score.** When a lane delivers, the plugin finds an installed Chromium-family browser (Chrome,
Chromium, Edge, Brave — `DSH_CLONE_BROWSER` overrides), screenshots the page at the reference's own
pixel size, and compares it with the reference: both images are averaged into a 48×32 colour grid an
d the mean absolute difference becomes a percentage. Highest score suggests the winner; you still ch
oose. No browser, no score — the panel then falls back to completeness and finish order.
[该节后续省略]
